# Gigwatt

> Gigwatt is an AI-run recruiting company placing electricians, low-voltage techs, pipefitters and related skilled
> trades on US data center, energy and industrial construction projects. Employers pay a flat $2,500
> per hire with a 30-day replacement guarantee; workers never pay.

## Key facts
- Price: $2,500 per hire, invoiced after 14 days on site, due in 15 days. No upfront fee or contract.
- Guarantee: free replacement if the hire leaves within 30 days.
- Workers: free; matched by text only to jobs that meet their trade, area and minimum rate; profile shared only after
  they say yes.
- Focus markets: Northern Virginia, Texas, Ohio, Arizona, Georgia, Iowa, Nevada.
- Updated: 2026-10-29

Questions, answered
What is Gigwatt?
Gigwatt is an AI-run recruiting company for skilled trades on data center, energy and industrial builds. AI agents find contractors who are hiring, source and screen electricians, low-voltage techs and pipefitters by text, and send the contractor interview-ready introductions. A person reviews every introduction.
How much does it cost to hire through Gigwatt?
Gigwatt charges a flat $2,500 per hire, invoiced after the worker has been on site for 14 days and due in 15 days. There is no upfront fee, no contract and nothing to pay if you don't hire.
Is Gigwatt free for electricians and other tradespeople?
Yes. Workers never pay. Employers pay the placement fee, and a worker's profile is only shared with an employer after the worker says yes to that specific job.
How is Gigwatt different from a staffing agency?
Traditional agencies typically charge 15-25% of first-year pay for a direct hire, or a 30-60% markup on temporary labor. Gigwatt charges a flat $2,500 per hire, the worker joins your payroll, and there's no contract to negotiate for the first hire.

## Gigwatt FAQ: Cost, Speed, Trades and How Matching Works
URL: https://gigwatt.co/faq/

Frequently asked questions
Gigwatt places electricians and other skilled trades on data center and energy builds. Employers pay $2,500 per hire; workers never pay.
What is Gigwatt?
Gigwatt is an AI-run recruiting company for skilled trades on data center, energy and industrial builds. AI agents find contractors who are hiring, source and screen electricians, low-voltage techs and pipefitters by text, and send the contractor interview-ready introductions. A person reviews every introduction.
How much does it cost to hire through Gigwatt?
Gigwatt charges a flat $2,500 per hire, invoiced after the worker has been on site for 14 days and due in 15 days. There is no upfront fee, no contract and nothing to pay if you don't hire.
Is Gigwatt free for electricians and other tradespeople?
Yes. Workers never pay. Employers pay the placement fee, and a worker's profile is only shared with an employer after the worker says yes to that specific job.
Which trades does Gigwatt place?
Mainly electricians (apprentice, journeyman, foreman and superintendent), low-voltage and structured-cabling techs, fiber splicers, pipefitters and steamfitters, and instrumentation and controls techs, plus millwrights, welders and ironworkers for the same projects.
Where does Gigwatt operate?
Across the United States, with a focus on data center and energy hubs: Northern Virginia (Ashburn, Manassas, Richmond), Texas (Dallas, Abilene, San Antonio), Ohio (Columbus, New Albany), Phoenix, Atlanta, Council Bluffs and Reno.
How fast can Gigwatt find workers?
Sourcing starts the minute a request arrives, and the goal is the first screened candidates within 72 hours. Speed depends on the trade, the location and whether the pay meets what local workers are asking.
How is Gigwatt different from a staffing agency?
Traditional agencies typically charge 15-25% of first-year pay for a direct hire, or a 30-60% markup on temporary labor. Gigwatt charges a flat $2,500 per hire, the worker joins your payroll, and there's no contract to negotiate for the first hire.
What happens if a hire doesn't work out?
If a placed worker leaves within 30 days of the start date, Gigwatt finds a replacement for free. If the invoice hasn't gone out yet, nothing is billed for that hire; if it has, it is credited.
How does Gigwatt screen candidates?
By text: trade and level, where they live and whether they travel, their minimum hourly rate, licences and certifications, and when they can start. Credentials are self-reported, so the employer verifies them before hiring. Each introduction explains why the candidate was matched.
Does AI make hiring decisions at Gigwatt?
No. AI helps read messages, ask screening questions and estimate fit from job-relevant facts only; names, contact details and protected characteristics are removed before scoring. The employer makes every hiring decision.
How do workers get matched to jobs?
Sign up at gigwatt.co/work or text us your trade, city and minimum rate. Gigwatt only texts you when a job fits your trade, area and pay floor. Reply YES to be introduced, NO to skip, or STOP at any time.
Does Gigwatt work with union contractors?
Most Gigwatt employers are merit-shop (open-shop) electrical and mechanical subcontractors. On union jobs, workers are usually dispatched through the local hall instead.
Hire workers Find work
Updated 2026-10-29.

## How to Hire Electricians for a Data Center Project (2026 Guide) | Gigwatt
URL: https://gigwatt.co/guides/hire-data-center-electricians/

How to hire electricians for a data center project
Short answer: electricians are the scarcest trade on data center builds, so the fastest route is to go
where they already are (job boards, traveler networks, other contractors' crews) with a pay rate that beats their current
job, screen quickly by text, and decide within days. Gigwatt does that for a flat $2,500 per hire.
Why it's hard right now
Data center construction spending hit a record $50.7 billion seasonally adjusted annual rate in April 2026 (U.S. Census Bureau data, via ThinkSet/BRG).
Electrical work typically takes 45-70% of a data center's construction budget, so electricians are the bottleneck.
Estimates of the 2026 US construction labor gap range from about 349,000 to 499,000 workers, and a licensed electrician takes 4-5 years to train.
Data center craft workers averaged about $81,800 a year in early 2026, roughly 32% more than on comparable commercial builds (Skillit), so they move for pay.
Your options compared
Option Typical cost Speed Who does the work
Recruit in-house Job ads plus recruiter time Weeks Your office staff
Staffing agency, temp labor 30-60% markup on hourly pay Days to weeks Agency recruiters
Staffing agency, direct hire 15-25% of first-year pay Weeks Agency recruiters
Union hall (signatory contractors) Per agreement Depends on the hall's out-of-work list Local hall
Gigwatt $2,500 per hire, after 14 days on site First screened candidates targeted within 72 hours AI agents, with a person reviewing every intro
What to put in a job request
Trade, level and headcount: "8 journeyman electricians and 1 foreman."
Location and travel: the site's city and state, and whether travelers are welcome.
Pay and per diem: an hourly range plus any daily per diem. Posts with real numbers get far more replies.
Requirements: licences and certifications such as OSHA 30, NFPA 70E or a state journeyman licence.
Start date and duration: "start Nov 17, 6+ months."
How Gigwatt works
Send one message with the details above.
Agents find and text matching workers and screen them on trade, location, pay floor and credentials.
You get interview-ready intros by email with why each candidate fits. Reply HIRED or PASS.
You pay $2,500 after the hire has worked 14 days, with a free replacement if they leave within 30 days.
Request workers Read the FAQ
Updated 2026-10-29. Market figures as cited; agency rates are typical industry ranges.

## Data Center Electrician Jobs: Pay, Travel and How to Get Hired (2026) | Gigwatt
URL: https://gigwatt.co/guides/data-center-electrician-jobs/

Data center electrician jobs: pay, travel and how to get hired
Short answer: data center projects pay electricians more than most commercial work, often with per diem
for travelers, and contractors are short-handed in Virginia, Texas, Ohio, Arizona and Georgia. Tell Gigwatt your trade,
city and minimum rate once and we text you only when a job beats it. It's free.
What the jobs pay
Data center craft workers averaged about $81,800 a year in early 2026, roughly 32% more than on comparable commercial
builds (Skillit). Pay depends on level, state and whether you travel. Check current hourly rates from real job posts on our
pay pages , for example electricians in Virginia.
Where the work is
Northern Virginia: Ashburn, Manassas, Richmond
Texas: Dallas, Abilene, San Antonio
Ohio: Columbus, New Albany
Arizona: Phoenix
Georgia: Atlanta
Iowa and Nevada: Council Bluffs, Reno
What employers ask for
Level and years: journeyman and foreman roles are the most in demand; apprentices get hired too.
Safety cards: OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 show up on most posts we see; NFPA 70E for energized work.
Low-voltage and fiber: structured cabling experience, BICSI credentials and fiber splicing.
A state licence where the work is, and a willingness to travel for traveler roles.
How to get matched
Sign up at gigwatt.co/work (2 minutes) or text us.
We ask a few quick questions by text: trade, level, location, minimum rate, certs.
When a job fits, we text you the details. Reply YES and we send your profile to that employer; NO to skip; STOP any time.
Find me jobs See open jobs
Updated 2026-10-29. Pay figure as cited.
